identity.name: Ivanti Connect Secure Pre-Auth IF-T Overflow to Internal Windows Pivot (SPAWN / CL-UNK-0979)
identity.summary: A pre-auth Ivanti Connect Secure IF-T overflow (CVE-2025-0282), appliance log-wipe, and pivot to an internal Windows host (DcomSrv service, /mail scheduled task, LSASS dump via hollowed svchost). The card's value: XDM modeling rules normalize the appliance IF-T telemetry so a correlation stitches the appliance source IP to the first internal host — a chain an EDR-only stack cannot produce.
identity.description: Modeled on Unit 42's CVE-2025-0282 / CVE-2025-0283 Ivanti Connect Secure exploitation reporting (activity cluster CL-UNK-0979, tactical overlap with Mandiant UNC5337). An unauthenticated attacker exploits a stack-based buffer overflow in Ivanti Connect Secure's IF-T (IF-T binding to TLS) handling to gain RCE on the VPN appliance with no credentials, then deploys the SPAWN malware family (SPAWNMOLE tunneler, SPAWNSNAIL SSH backdoor, SPAWNSLOTH log-tamperer), runs the ldap.pl Perl script to decrypt appliance-stored credentials, and pivots via RDP to an internal Windows host. On that host the operator establishes persistence with a service named DcomSrv (vixDiskLib.dll side-loaded by the legitimate vmdisk.exe, its embedded description carrying the misspelled string DCOMLIENT) and a scheduled task named /mail (deelevator64.dll side-loaded by DeElevate64.exe), dumps LSASS memory with package.dll (built via MSBuild.exe compiling mini.xml, XOR-encoded output written to C:\Users\Public\Downloads\VM.txt), injects into a suspended svchost.exe via process hollowing, and beacons to 168.100.8[.]144 and 193.149.180[.]128. The appliance side is scrubbed: log.events.vc0 and debuglog deleted, /var/cores emptied. The detection emphasis is the XDM modeling-rule SUBSTRATE: an EDR-only stack sees the Windows persistence but has no appliance telemetry, so it cannot know the DcomSrv host was reached from a pre-auth VPN exploit. This card authors two modeling rules that normalize the raw Ivanti appliance IF-T debug/syslog and log-tampering file-audit telemetry into addressable XDM fields (xdm.source.ipv4, xdm.event.description, xdm.target.file.path); those modeled fields make the pre-auth 'Invalid IFT packet received from unauthenticated client' tell and the anonymization-infrastructure source IPs (185.219.141[.]95 NordVPN node, 185.195.71[.]244 Tor exit) searchable, and a correlation rule then stitches the modeled appliance-plane signal to the endpoint-plane Windows-persistence BIOCs into one incident — the cross-source stitch that is the whole point of an analytics platform over a single-plane EDR. A modeling rule does not itself fire; it ENABLES firing, so it is counted informationally, not as a seventh detection_type.

campaigns: Ivanti Connect Secure CVE-2025-0282 pre-auth exploitation (December 2024 onward)

techniques.name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-MP-010 — Ivanti pre-auth IF-T overflow to internal Windows pivot, XDM modeling-rule substrate + appliance-to-endpoint correlation stitch

prerequisites.description: The Ivanti Connect Secure appliance forwards syslog/debug telemetry to Cortex XSIAM as a raw source (ivanti_ics_raw) so the modeling rules have raw events to normalize.
Cortex XDR / XSIAM agent installed on the internal Windows pivot host so DcomSrv service creation and LSASS-dump telemetry reaches xdr_data.

payload.code:
# NON-DESTRUCTIVE emulation. No real overflow, no memory read, no deletion.
# Emit SAFE-MODE marker artifacts that mirror the observable shapes the
# Ivanti appliance and the internal Windows pivot host would produce, so the
# modeling rules, BIOCs, and the appliance-to-endpoint correlation can be
# exercised in a lab without any appliance or Windows target.
set -euo pipefail
WORK="${WORK_DIR:-/tmp/cortexsim-mp-010}"
mkdir -p "$WORK"
# (1) appliance IF-T pre-auth exploitation tell + anonymization source IP
printf '%s\n' 'Invalid IFT packet received from unauthenticated client src=185.219.141.95' > "$WORK/ivanti-debug.log"
# (2) Windows persistence: DcomSrv service via vixDiskLib.dll side-load (marker)
printf '%s\n' 'service=DcomSrv binary=vmdisk.exe module=vixDiskLib.dll desc=DCOMLIENT' > "$WORK/dcomsrv-service.marker"
# (3) /mail scheduled task launching DeElevate64.exe (marker)
printf '%s\n' 'schtask=/mail action=DeElevate64.exe module=deelevator64.dll' > "$WORK/mail-task.marker"
# (4) LSASS dump SAFE-MODE marker (no memory is read)
printf '%s\n' 'SAFE-MODE marker only — package.dll VM.txt dump NOT performed' > "$WORK/VM.txt"
echo '[CortexSim] SIM-MP-010 safe-mode emulation complete.'

input_variables.name: WORK_DIR
input_variables.description: Directory the SAFE-MODE marker artifacts are written to.

expected_artifacts.description: Appliance debug-log line carrying the pre-auth IF-T exploitation tell and an anonymization-infrastructure source IP, normalized by the modeling rule into xdm.event.description + xdm.source.ipv4.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: message contains "Invalid IFT packet received from unauthenticated client"

expected_artifacts.description: Internal Windows host: a service named DcomSrv created via vixDiskLib.dll side-loaded by vmdisk.exe.

iocs.context: ldap.pl — custom Perl credential-harvesting script that decrypts Ivanti appliance-stored passwords, used for RDP lateral movement (T1003 / T1133).
package.dll — memory-dumping tool built via MSBuild.exe compiling mini.xml; XOR-encodes the LSASS dump (key 0x27) to C:\Users\Public\Downloads\VM.txt (T1003.001).
vixDiskLib.dll — DLL side-loading backdoor loaded by the legitimate vmdisk.exe; creates the DcomSrv service and process-hollows a suspended svchost.exe (T1574.002 / T1543.003).
deelevator64.dll — DLL side-loading backdoor loaded by DeElevate64.exe, triggered by the /mail scheduled task (T1053.005 / T1574.002).
C2 endpoint the injected svchost.exe beacons to after process hollowing on the internal Windows host.
Second C2 endpoint the hollowed svchost.exe beacons to.
NordVPN node seen in Ivanti appliance debug logs sourcing 'Invalid IFT packet received from unauthenticated client' pre-auth exploitation attempts.
Tor exit node seen in Ivanti appliance debug logs sourcing the pre-auth IF-T exploitation attempts.
Drop path of the package.dll memory-dumping tool on the internal Windows pivot host.

modeling_rules.name: Ivanti Connect Secure Appliance IF-T Telemetry Normalization
modeling_rules.description: Normalizes the raw Ivanti Connect Secure appliance debug/syslog stream (ivanti_ics_raw) into addressable XDM fields so the pre-auth IF-T exploitation tell and the attacker source IP become searchable and stitchable. Raw vendor fields map as: source_address -> xdm.source.ipv4, client_hostname -> xdm.source.host.hostname, appliance_hostname -> xdm.target.host.hostname, message -> xdm.event.description, auth_result -> xdm.event.outcome. This modeling rule is the normalization SUBSTRATE beneath the appliance-to-endpoint correlation — it enables firing, it does not itself fire.
modeling_rules.logic:
[MODEL: dataset = ivanti_ics_raw]
| alter xdm.source.ipv4 = source_address
| alter xdm.source.host.hostname = client_hostname
| alter xdm.target.host.hostname = appliance_hostname
| alter xdm.event.description = message
| alter xdm.event.outcome = auth_result
| alter xdm.observer.type = "vpn-gateway"
| filter xdm.event.description contains "IFT" or xdm.event.description contains "IF-T"

modeling_rules.name: Ivanti Appliance Log-Tampering File-Event Normalization
modeling_rules.description: Normalizes the Ivanti appliance file-audit sub-stream so the SPAWNSLOTH log-tampering deletions become addressable XDM file events. Raw vendor fields map as: file_path -> xdm.target.file.path, file_operation -> xdm.event.operation, source_address -> xdm.source.ipv4. Filters to the specific appliance logs the intrusion wipes (log.events.vc0, debuglog) and the emptied /var/cores. Substrate only — enables the defense-evasion detection, does not fire itself.
modeling_rules.logic:
[MODEL: dataset = ivanti_ics_raw]
| filter event_type = "file_audit"
| alter xdm.target.file.path = file_path
| alter xdm.target.file.filename = arrayindex(split(file_path, "/"), -1)
| alter xdm.event.operation = file_operation
| alter xdm.source.ipv4 = source_address
| filter xdm.target.file.path in ("/data/runtime/logs/log.events.vc0", "/data/var/dlogs/debuglog", "/var/cores")
| filter xdm.event.operation in ("DELETE", "TRUNCATE")

biocs.name: Ivanti-to-Windows Pivot: DcomSrv Service Created via vixDiskLib DLL Sideload
biocs.description: Fires on the internal Windows pivot host only when BOTH SPAWN-family signals are present on the same host: (1) vixDiskLib.dll is side-loaded by the legitimate vmdisk.exe as an UNSIGNED module or from outside Program Files — the anomaly that distinguishes the attacker-supplied DLL from the legitimate VMware VDDK library that vmdisk.exe normally loads — modeled on a MODULE_LOAD event; and (2) a service named DcomSrv is created. Requiring the load anomaly AND the DcomSrv persistence together avoids firing on normal VMware/Veeam backup activity, and keying on module + service name rather than a hash survives repacking.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter (event_type = ENUM.MODULE and event_sub_type = ENUM.MODULE_LOAD and action_module_name contains "vixDiskLib.dll" and actor_process_image_name = "vmdisk.exe" and (action_module_signature_status = "UNSIGNED" or action_module_path not contains "Program Files")) or (event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START and action_process_image_name in ("sc.exe", "services.exe", "vmdisk.exe") and action_process_image_command_line contains "DcomSrv")
| alter dcom_signal = if(event_type = ENUM.MODULE, "vixdisklib_anomalous_sideload", "dcomsrv_service_create")
| comp count_distinct(dcom_signal) as dcom_signals by agent_hostname
| filter dcom_signals >= 2
| fields agent_hostname, dcom_signals

biocs.name: Ivanti-to-Windows Pivot: /mail Scheduled Task Launching DeElevate64
biocs.description: Fires when a scheduled task named /mail launches DeElevate64.exe (which side-loads deelevator64.dll) on the internal Windows pivot host — the second SPAWN-family persistence mechanism. Keys on the /mail task name plus the DeElevate64 launcher.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "schtasks.exe" or actor_process_image_name = "svchost.exe"
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains "/mail" and action_process_image_command_line contains "DeElevate64"
| comp count() as sched_task_events by agent_hostname
| filter sched_task_events >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, sched_task_events

biocs.name: Ivanti-to-Windows Pivot: LSASS Memory Dump via Hollowed svchost
biocs.description: Fires when at least two of the credential-dump observables are seen on one host, each modeled on its real event type: (1) an LSASS handle opened with read/query rights (PROCESS_ACCESS against lsass.exe with PROCESS_VM_READ|PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION); (2) process hollowing into a suspended svchost.exe (PROCESS_ACCESS against svchost.exe with PROCESS_VM_WRITE|PROCESS_CREATE_THREAD rights); and (3) the XOR-encoded dump written to C:\Users\Public\Downloads\VM.txt (FILE write). Requiring two distinct real observables avoids the dead PROCESS_START/action_file_path match the earlier body degraded to.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter (event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_ACCESS and target_process_name = "lsass.exe" and requested_access bitand 0x0410 != 0) or (event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_ACCESS and target_process_name = "svchost.exe" and requested_access bitand 0x0022 != 0 and causality_actor_process_image_name not in ("services.exe", "svchost.exe")) or (event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type in (ENUM.FILE_CREATE_NEW, ENUM.FILE_WRITE) and action_file_path contains "C:\Users\Public\Downloads\VM.txt")
| alter dump_signal = if(event_type = ENUM.FILE, "vm_txt_dump_write", if(target_process_name = "lsass.exe", "lsass_handle_open", "svchost_hollow_inject"))
| comp count_distinct(dump_signal) as dump_signals, values(causality_actor_process_image_name) as injector_images by agent_hostname
| filter dump_signals >= 2
| fields agent_hostname, dump_signals, injector_images

xql_queries.name: Ivanti IF-T Pre-Auth Exploitation Tell Modeled from Appliance Telemetry
xql_queries.query:
dataset = ivanti_ics_raw
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 3600)
| filter message contains "Invalid IFT packet received from unauthenticated client"
| alter src_ip = source_address
| filter src_ip in ("185.219.141.95", "185.195.71.244")
| comp count() as preauth_tells by src_ip
| filter preauth_tells >= 1
| fields src_ip, preauth_tells

xql_queries.name: Appliance Source IP Stitched to Internal Windows Pivot Host
xql_queries.query:
dataset = ivanti_ics_raw
| filter message contains "Invalid IFT packet received from unauthenticated client"
| alter signal = "appliance_preauth_exploit", entity = source_address
| fields signal, entity, _time
| union (
    dataset = xdr_data
    | filter action_process_image_command_line contains "DcomSrv" or action_process_image_command_line contains "DeElevate64"
    | alter signal = "internal_windows_persistence", entity = agent_hostname
    | fields signal, entity, _time
)
| comp count() as observations by signal
| filter observations >= 1
| fields signal, observations

correlation_rules.name: Ivanti Pre-Auth Compromise Stitched to Internal Windows Persistence
correlation_rules.logic: XQL(Ivanti IF-T Pre-Auth Exploitation Tell Modeled from Appliance Telemetry) AND (BIOC(Ivanti-to-Windows Pivot: DcomSrv Service Created via vixDiskLib DLL Sideload) OR BIOC(Ivanti-to-Windows Pivot: /mail Scheduled Task Launching DeElevate64) OR BIOC(Ivanti-to-Windows Pivot: LSASS Memory Dump via Hollowed svchost)) — fires when the modeled Ivanti appliance pre-auth exploitation tell (source IP from anonymization infrastructure) is observed within a 24h window of any internal Windows persistence BIOC, stitching the appliance-plane and endpoint-plane signal into one incident an EDR-only stack cannot assemble because it has no appliance telemetry.

analytics_modules.module: Cortex XSIAM Analytics — cross-source causality stitching (appliance-plane to endpoint-plane)
analytics_modules.note: Backed by correlation CR-MP-0014, which fuses the modeled Ivanti IF-T appliance tell (XQL) with the internal-Windows persistence BIOCs.

products.evidence_query: In Xpanse / XSIAM ASM, filter Attack Surface Rules to 'Insecure Pulse Secure Pulse Connect Secure VPN' to enumerate internet-exposed Ivanti/Pulse appliances that are candidate CVE-2025-0282 targets before the exploit lands.

dataset = xdr_data | filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START | filter action_process_image_command_line contains "DcomSrv" or action_module_path contains "vixDiskLib.dll" | fields agent_hostname, action_process_image_name, action_process_image_command_line

dataset = ivanti_ics_raw | filter message contains "Invalid IFT packet received from unauthenticated client" | alter src_ip = source_address | union (dataset = xdr_data | filter action_process_image_command_line contains "DcomSrv" | alter src_ip = agent_hostname) | fields src_ip, _time

threat_scenarios.name: Appliance-to-Endpoint Stitch via XDM Modeling — Ivanti Pre-Auth to Internal Windows Pivot
threat_scenarios.description: A DC proves that normalizing raw VPN-appliance telemetry into XDM is what lets Cortex stitch a pre-auth appliance compromise to the first internal Windows host — the cross-plane chain a single-plane EDR cannot produce. Modeling rules make the Ivanti IF-T tell addressable; endpoint BIOCs catch the SPAWN-family persistence; a correlation rule fuses them.

threat_steps.objective: The XDM modeling rules normalize raw Ivanti appliance telemetry and the validation XQL surfaces the pre-auth IF-T exploitation tell with an anonymization-infrastructure source IP.
preconditions: Ivanti Connect Secure appliance forwarding syslog/debug telemetry to XSIAM as ivanti_ics_raw.
The IF-T telemetry modeling rule applied.
steps: Apply MODEL-MP-IVANTI-IFT to normalize ivanti_ics_raw into XDM fields.
Emit / observe the 'Invalid IFT packet received from unauthenticated client' debug line.
Run the validation XQL and confirm the modeled source IP is returned.
success_criteria: Validation XQL `Ivanti IF-T Pre-Auth Exploitation Tell Modeled from Appliance Telemetry` returns >= 1 row.
The returned src_ip is one of the anonymization-infrastructure IPs (185.219.141.95 / 185.195.71.244).

threat_steps.objective: The internal-Windows persistence BIOCs fire on the pivot host for the SPAWN-family DcomSrv service, /mail scheduled task, and LSASS dump.
preconditions: Cortex agent installed on the internal Windows pivot host.
The DcomSrv / /mail / LSASS-dump observables present in xdr_data.
steps: Observe DcomSrv service creation via vixDiskLib.dll side-load.
Observe the /mail scheduled task launching DeElevate64.exe.
Observe the MSBuild/mini.xml LSASS dump to VM.txt.
success_criteria: BIOC `Ivanti-to-Windows Pivot: DcomSrv Service Created via vixDiskLib DLL Sideload` fires.
BIOC `Ivanti-to-Windows Pivot: /mail Scheduled Task Launching DeElevate64` fires.
BIOC `Ivanti-to-Windows Pivot: LSASS Memory Dump via Hollowed svchost` fires.

threat_steps.objective: The correlation rule stitches the modeled appliance-plane tell to the endpoint-plane persistence into one incident — the EDR-only-can't-do-this proof.
preconditions: TC-MP-010A and TC-MP-010B observables present within the correlation window.
steps: Let both the modeled appliance tell and an internal Windows persistence BIOC land within 24h.
Observe CR-MP-0014 raise one stitched incident linking the appliance source IP to the internal pivot host.
success_criteria: Correlation `CR-MP-0014` raises exactly one stitched appliance-to-endpoint incident.
The incident links the appliance source IP to the internal Windows pivot hostname.

preventive_controls: Patch Ivanti Connect Secure to 22.7R2.5+ (Policy Secure 22.7R1.2+, Neurons for ZTA 22.7R2.3+) to close CVE-2025-0282 / CVE-2025-0283; run the Ivanti Integrity Checker Tool on any appliance exposed before patching.
Front internet-facing VPN appliances with NGFW Advanced Threat Prevention (signature 95948 covers the IF-T exploitation) and restrict management-plane exposure.
Deny interactive/RDP lateral movement from appliance-adjacent segments and require phishing-resistant MFA on internal Windows hosts.
Enforce DLL-load allow-listing so legitimate binaries (vmdisk.exe, DeElevate64.exe) cannot side-load attacker DLLs from writable paths.
detection_engineering: Author XDM modeling rules for VPN-appliance syslog/debug sources BEFORE relying on any appliance detection — un-modeled appliance logs are searchable but not analytics-grade or stitchable.
Alert on the pre-auth 'Invalid IFT packet received from unauthenticated client' tell, especially from anonymization infrastructure (NordVPN / Tor exit nodes).
Alert on deletion/truncation of appliance logs (log.events.vc0, debuglog, /var/cores) as a log-tampering indicator.
Correlate appliance-plane compromise signal with endpoint-plane persistence (DcomSrv service, /mail scheduled task, LSASS dump) to reconstruct the appliance-to-host pivot an EDR-only stack misses.
